items.description: The new rule closes a loophole that existed that allowed Chinese companies to still access advanced AI chips remotely, despite U.S. restrictions on their physical sale to China.

items.title: Lindsay Clancy to face a new trial in spring of 2027 over children's killing
items.description: A new trial is set in Massachusetts against Lindsay Clancy as prosecutors seek a criminal conviction over the killing of her three young children.

items.title: These birds fly 17,000 miles every year. Climate change could make it harder
items.description: Migratory birds cross the entire globe, carefully timing their journeys with the seasons. In a hotter climate, that timing is increasingly out of sync.

items.title: Far from home. Voyager 1 is now farther than anything man has sent into space
items.description: NASA's Voyager 1, which is the furthest man-made object from Earth, is set to reach a new milestone this week. On Wednesday, the probe will be roughly 16 billion miles from Earth.

items.title: SpaceX successfully catches Starship and makes history
items.description: The company's spacecraft returned to its Texas launchpad in dramatic fashion — by carefully lowering itself until two metal arms attached to the launch tower could secure it.

items.title: SpaceX deploys Starlink satellites in Starship test, but booster crashes into Gulf
items.description: SpaceX conducted a major test of its Starship rocket Friday night. It deployed several satellites for the Starlink constellation, but there was a problem with its booster.

items.title: SpaceX's giant rocket may leave NASA in the dust
items.description: As it races to develop its new massive rocket, the space launch company is preparing to retire NASA's main ride to the International Space Station.

items.title: Scientists think they've found ancient remnants of dinosaur blood
items.description: Scientists have studied plenty of dinosaur bones, eggs and footprints. Now, some think they've found their strongest evidence yet of dinosaur blood.

items.title: Mice can learn to fight by watching tiny rodent cage matches, study finds
items.description: Brain scientists set up "gladiator style" cage matches for mice — and found that simply observing fighting matches can rewire a mouse's brain to resemble those who actually fought.

items.title: Why sleep matters when it comes to weight gain and loss
items.description: Sleep can have a powerful impact on weight. Research shows it can affect appetite. There is also a two-way relationship between sleep quality and diet.

items.title: What's the real cost of fast fashion? Ask the people making your jeans
items.description: Sydney Sweeney has great jeans, American Eagle Outfitters tells us. But who made them? And what are working conditions like in the garment factories of Pakistan and Bangladesh?

items.title: Laws limiting coal miners' exposure to toxic dust are in danger of being rolled back
items.description: Coal miners who are exposed to silica dust are at a higher risk of black lung disease. Despite decades of advocacy, new efforts to regulate the toxic dust are under threat.

items.title: A new generation of disability rights activists carry on Judy Heumann's legacy
items.description: The film Being Heumann tells the lesser-known story of the mother of the disability rights movement. A new generation of activists share how they "carry the torch" today.

items.title: US has lost measles elimination status, global health authorities say
items.description: The U.S. has lost its status as a country where measles is eliminated, according to researchers with direct knowledge of the deliberations at the Pan American Health Organization.
